A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SepLLM and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Existing material can be matched reliably; v4 adds Appendices G–I.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark scores, training losses, streaming perplexity and timing measurements, ablations and retrieval experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports original empirical results in Tables 1–13 and the training, retrieval and attention figures, including results retained from v1.

M1.justification: The causal attention mask, initial/separator/neighboring token selection, streaming cache management and positional shifting remain unchanged. The encoder and hardmax constructions added in the appendices serve the theoretical analysis rather than revising the evaluated procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Pile and LongAlpaca training coverage and the same GSM8K-CoT, MMLU, ARC, LAMBADA, LogiQA, PIQA, SciQ, PG19, WikiText and Needle In A Haystack evaluations.

E2.justification: Vanilla/full attention and StreamingLLM, abbreviated StrmLLM, retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. No additional cited method becomes an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Reported model configurations, shots, training budgets, checkpoints, metrics and experimental cache settings are retained. Added cache-parameter disclosures clarify existing experiments without establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 5(a) slightly revises late-training loss evidence used in the neighboring-window and hybrid-layer ablations. The variants, questions and conclusions remain unchanged, as do the WikiText sensitivity tests and appendix generalization and retrieval studies.

E5.justification: The reporting practices remain unchanged, with no added run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Small changes in plotted loss values do not establish a change in uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Late-stage loss traces change slightly in Figure 5(a) and Figure 1's training-time panel, without changing the broad trends. Tables 1–13 retain their numerical results; Table 9's 620.3 becoming 620.30 is equivalent formatting. Retrieval and attention-map results are unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 adds Appendices G–H, stating an encoder-based universal-approximation theorem under bidirectional local attention and bounded separator gaps. It introduces function classes, contextual mapping, quantization and several proof lemmas absent from v1. Section 3.3 also explicitly states the cache constraint a + s + w < c.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal segment-compression, acceleration and long-streaming claims remain unchanged, including the headline KV-cache and training-efficiency claims. Calling SepLLM a new language-modeling perspective mainly reframes its existing contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds a specific mechanism argument: successful retrieval despite discarding nonseparator needle-token KV supports compression into separators. v1 already reports retrieval and its general compression interpretation, but lacks this explicit reasoning.

D1.justification: v4 specifies w=224 for Table 4, clarifies StreamingLLM's initial-cache setting in Appendix D's architecture comparison, and adds a Needle In A Haystack implementation reference. These are documentation additions; the project's existing code-access information remains.

R1.justification: v4 adds Yun et al. (2020) on universal approximability of sparse Transformers and explicitly builds its proof on that work. The existing related-work coverage and positioning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 polishes grammar and terminology throughout, revises portions of the conclusion, corrects Seg-Attention to Sep-Attention, and adds appendix cross-references and an AI-editing disclosure. The established main-section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 3–4 are redrawn with clearer lettering, baseline legend spelling is corrected, and several captions are refined. Existing appendix figures move behind the added theory while retaining their content. The figure/table inventory and overall layout remain stable.

improvement.justification: Clearer diagrams, copyediting and added cache settings offer limited benefits. However, the main addition concerns an encoder variant, and Lemma H.4 contains an internal sign inconsistency: its definition of Phi gives min-minus-max on the stated interval, while the following expression uses max-minus-min. The theoretical benefit therefore remains unresolved. With empirical changes limited, these competing effects prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
